question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,4],$ compute $P(W\ge 1).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $W$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le w\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,4],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(w)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4},\, & 0\le w\le 4, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W\ge 1) & =P(1\le W\le 4) \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}f(w)\,\text{d}w \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}w \\  & =\frac{4-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
